verified: The failure is page-specific, not language-specific or model-specific: same 3 pages fail identically under both professionalize_llm and m2m100_418m across 5 distinct languages.

src/translation_engine/validation/structure_validator.py::_count_code_blocks (line 230) sums fenced-code-block count AND inline-backtick-span count into one total, then _check_code_blocks (line ~217) raises ValidationSeverity.ERROR (hard reject, result.success=False) on ANY mismatch between source and translation totals -- unlike headings/lists/links, which are WARNING/INFO only.

The 3 failing pages are Go API reference/developer-guide content saturated with inline code identifiers (e.g. features.md has 41 backtick-delimited spans like `Workbook`, `Cell.SetStyle`, `DataValidationTypeWhole` in ~300 lines); the 1 succeeding page (developer-guide/_index.md) is comparatively prose-heavy with far fewer inline code spans.

SOURCE-SIDE SMOKING GUN (checked directly against the on-disk English source, no translated text needed): _count_code_blocks's inline regex r"`[^`]+`" is applied to the WHOLE document text, including inside fenced ```go blocks -- it does not exclude fenced-block regions before counting inline spans. features.md's fenced Go code contains a Go raw-string literal, `"Apple,Banana,Cherry,Dragonfruit"`, i.e. LITERAL BACKTICKS inside the fence (line ~191); working-with-spreadsheet-management.md's fences contain 6 more backtick occurrences. The succeeding page's only fenced block (a `func main(){...}` Hello World, no string literals) contains ZERO backticks inside it. This cleanly separates the failing pages from the succeeding one by a mechanism that has nothing to do with translation quality: any Go code sample using backtick raw-string syntax already inflates the source-side inline-code count in a way coupled to exactly how the fenced block's content renders, so a translation that reproduces the code block with even benign whitespace/formatting drift (or that touches the fence boundary) is highly likely to produce a different total and hit the ERROR-severity hard reject -- independent of whether any real API identifier was mistranslated.
unverified: Still not directly confirmed from actual model OUTPUT (no stored translated text per mission rule) whether the count drift in these specific rejections was literally the fenced-block-backtick mechanism above vs. a genuinely dropped identifier elsewhere in the same page -- the source-side analysis makes the fenced-block mechanism the prime suspect but a live-instrumented rerun (approach A below) is needed to close the loop with certainty.

Whether this is the SAME root-cause class as any already-tracked heal_queue entry -- the auto-classifier labels these tickets root_cause_class=auto:LinkValidator (picks a different validator name than the actual ERROR-severity one, StructureValidator's code-block check), so this specific mechanism is not being surfaced as its own distinct, trackable class today.

hypothesis: StructureValidator._count_code_blocks (structure_validator.py:230-244) counts inline backtick spans across the ENTIRE text without first stripping fenced-code-block regions, so Go (and likely Rust/C++) code samples that use backtick-delimited raw string literals inside ``` fences inflate and destabilize the inline-code count independent of translation quality. Any page whose fenced code contains a literal backtick is then one benign code-block re-render away from a false-positive ERROR-severity hard reject on EVERY language. This class of page (API-reference content with code samples) is extremely common across the portfolio's largest remaining Tier-1a backlog: reference.aspose.org alone has 1,567 (pdf) + 664 (words) + 262 (3d) + 243 (cells) + 239 (html) = 2,975 zero-translation pages, almost certainly this exact shape.
two_approaches: A. Fix _count_code_blocks to strip fenced-code-block regions (regex-extract and remove ```...``` spans) BEFORE running the inline-backtick-span regex on what remains, so raw-string-literal backticks inside Go/Rust/C++ code samples never enter the inline-code tally in the first place. This is a validator-methodology fix, not a translation-preservation fix -- low risk, mirrors how the fenced-block counter already treats ``` specially.

B. Live-instrument one failing cell (features.md -> one language) the same way TC-APT-100 diagnosed its determiner-before-link bug, to positively confirm the mechanism before touching the validator, in case something else is also contributing.
chosen: Neither executed this iteration -- documenting only, per the mission rule that a new taskcard/root-cause investigation is Track-B scope, not something to rush inside a live Track-A wave. Recommend A as the actual fix (the source-side evidence already isolates the mechanism precisely enough to act on) with B's live-instrumented rerun as the verification step afterward, using features.md as the regression fixture either way. Given the portfolio-wide blast radius (reference.aspose.org's ~3000-page backlog is exactly this content shape), this deserves a new TC-APT taskcard rather than folding into TC-APT-042 (which is about sentence-structure defects, a different mechanism).
regression_control: Whichever fix lands, add a StructureValidator unit test fixture built from features.md's actual inline-code density pattern (multiple backtick spans per line, some adjacent) asserting the false-positive case from A is no longer hard-rejected, alongside a true-positive fixture (a genuinely dropped identifier) that must still reject.
